claims.claim: Didymus the Blind was born about 313 in Alexandria, Egypt, and died about 398 in Alexandria.
Didymus the Blind was an Eastern church theologian who headed the influential catechetical school of Alexandria.
Didymus the Blind was blind since childhood and remained a layman all his life.
Didymus the Blind was made head of the Alexandrian school by Athanasius the Great, bishop of Alexandria.
Didymus the Blind was a leading opponent of Arianism.

Didymus the Blind's works were condemned by the Second Council of Constantinople in 553 for teaching the doctrine of Origen, which caused most of his works not to be copied during the European Middle Ages and thus to be lost.
SCOPE: this English is Fragmenta in Psalmos from PG 39, the sections stored for didymus-fragmenta-psalmos. The Tura papyrus commentary is a different work.
Didymus's commentaries discuss long quotations from the Bible, and he interprets scriptures allegorically, seeing symbols everywhere.
